title: NERDs Fuzzing Guide
intro: Use this guide to learn the mechanics of coverage-guided fuzzing in the NERDs CLI. The steps explain how to operate the tools, not how to solve the assigned investigation.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.summary: Read the task description first. Work only in the assigned task workspace. A harness is a small program that supplies inputs to the target; a corpus is a saved collection of test inputs.

steps.detail: This is your editable workspace. Each task has its own copy of the source files.
Look at the Makefile, harnesses/, src/, and include/ before choosing a fuzzing target.
Builds the targets with the installed Clang 19 compiler and its libFuzzer/AddressSanitizer libraries. If the build fails, read the terminal error before making changes.

sections.heading: Understand and choose a harness
sections.summary: This task provides three executable harnesses: fuzz_a, fuzz_b, and fuzz_c. Each is compiled from its matching source file under harnesses/ and supplies inputs through a particular entry point. Examine their source to understand what they exercise; no harness is prescribed as the correct choice.

steps.detail: Read how this harness passes generated inputs to the program. The fuzz_a executable is built from this file.
Compare how this harness constructs or transforms the inputs it passes to the program. The fuzz_b executable is built from this file.
Inspect the input path and function calls made by this harness. The fuzz_c executable is built from this file.

sections.heading: Start fuzzing
sections.summary: Choose a harness after examining the three harness source files. The commands below demonstrate fuzz_a only; replace the executable and corpus directory when using fuzz_b or fuzz_c.

steps.detail: Keeping the corpus in ../runs lets you reuse its inputs instead of starting from scratch each time.
Runs libFuzzer for up to two minutes. Watch the output for runs, coverage, newly discovered inputs, and sanitizer errors. The collector records campaign activity.
Runs at most 100 executions when you want a quick sanity check without a longer timed campaign.

sections.heading: Stop and continue
sections.summary: You may stop a campaign and come back to the same harness. Keep your saved corpus between runs.

steps.detail: Click the CLI terminal and press Control+C. Wait for the program to return to the shell prompt; do not close or kill the container.
Using the same corpus directory starts another campaign seeded with the inputs already collected. The two-minute limit applies to this new run.
Create ../runs/corpus-b first with mkdir -p; keep the corpora separate for clarity.

sections.heading: Investigate outcomes
sections.summary: Use the terminal output and source files to decide what to try next; not every campaign will discover a crash.

steps.detail: Inspect corpora and other files you have saved during this task.
You may inspect and modify your task's editable files. Rebuild after source changes.
The fuzzer may save a crashing input in the current directory; preserve it and the terminal output. If there is no crash file, this command may report no match.

terms.definition: Code that feeds test inputs to the program or function being fuzzed.
A directory of saved test inputs (seeds) that libFuzzer can mutate and reuse between runs. Keep separate corpora for different harnesses.
A measure of the code paths or execution edges exercised by inputs.
An input saved after a failure; keep it for examination and reproduction.

notes: Use only the internal CLI and BROWSER tabs for study work. If you need AI or web search, open it inside the NERDs Browser so the study can capture relevant interactions.
To use a guide command, click Copy beside it, switch to CLI, and paste using Shift + Insert. The copy operation stays inside NERDs. Host-to-NERDs clipboard transfer remains restricted.
After each task, choose Finish Task if you believe you have finished, or Skip Task if you want to stop without finishing. Both choices preserve work and advance the study.
If a command fails, keep the output and try to understand the error. You are not required to find a crash.
